items.headline: Anthropic sets $70-$78 IPO price range, targeting $1.4T valuation
items.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $70-$78 per share for 825 million shares, potentially netting up to $64.35 billion in proceeds and valuing the company at up to $1.405 trillion on a fully diluted basis. The listing, planned for next week, would be one of the largest IPOs in history amid investor skepticism about AI valuations.

items.headline: Anthropic adds $26B private placement from tech giants to IPO
items.summary: Anthropic entered agreements with Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC to buy $26 billion of Class N common stock in a private placement alongside its IPO. Together with cornerstone investments, the total share offering will raise up to $90.4 billion.

items.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon frontier model
items.summary: Google launched Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier model specialized in long-horizon engineering and state-of-the-art cybersecurity defense, now available to developers, enterprises and consumers. It joins Gemini 4 Argon for complex coding and financial workflows in Google's expanding frontier lineup.

items.headline: Google debuts two specialized AI chips to broaden hardware portfolio
items.summary: Google launched new AI accelerators including the TPU 8i Max, which combines two inference-focused TPU 8i chips to double memory, processing power and bandwidth. The move comes as hyperscalers and AI labs build custom silicon to reduce reliance on Nvidia.

items.headline: Anthropic unveils Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models
items.summary: Anthropic released two new frontier models, with Fable 5.2 broadly available and Mythos 5.2 reserved for vetted cybersecurity and life sciences teams. The launch pairs record-high benchmarks with a 20% API cost reduction and marks Anthropic's first frontier release since CEO Dario Amodei called to slow AI development in September.

items.headline: CoreWeave earnings beat re-energizes AI trade, Nasdaq rises 2%
items.summary: CoreWeave beat Wall Street revenue expectations and raised 2026 guidance, sending its shares up 25% and lifting the Nasdaq 2% after a historic tech selloff. The neocloud provider's results eased investor fears about AI infrastructure spending.

items.headline: TSMC approves up to $1B investment in Anthropic and OpenAI
items.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. approved investments of up to $1 billion in AI companies Anthropic and OpenAI. The move deepens ties between the world's largest chipmaker and leading AI labs ahead of Anthropic's IPO.

items.headline: Rackspace and Together AI sign enterprise AI inference deal
items.summary: Rackspace and Together AI announced a multiyear strategic agreement under which Rackspace will provide dedicated NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 infrastructure to support Together AI inference workloads. Deployment is planned for 2027 as Rackspace positions itself as operator of the full enterprise AI stack.

items.headline: United Airlines bans AI bots from booking flights
items.summary: United Airlines said it will prevent personal AI assistants from accessing its systems to book tickets. The move signals growing tension between airlines and the emerging wave of agentic AI tools acting on consumers' behalf.

items.headline: Reuters: AI backlash could threaten Anthropic IPO timing
items.summary: Investors say rising public backlash against AI and a two-day market selloff following US midterm elections could pressure Anthropic to delay its offering. Prospective buyers are awaiting Anthropic's withheld October revenue figure to assess whether growth has rebounded.

items.headline: Google ships November Pixel Drop with Gemini Intelligence
items.summary: Google's November Pixel Drop brings Gemini Intelligence updates, custom widgets, and the launch of Pixel Tag across its devices. The update extends Google's on-device AI capabilities to the Pixel 10 lineup.

items.headline: Pennsylvania Democrats pledge crackdown on AI data centers
items.summary: After a campaign season of outrage against energy-hungry AI data centers, midterm wins ushered in Democrats pledging tougher regulation of the facilities. A stricter regulatory environment for AI giants and developers is expected to follow.

items.headline: US consumer sentiment improves but AI bubble worries emerge
items.summary: US consumer sentiment rose in November even as concerns about an AI bubble began to surface among respondents. The mixed signals reflect growing public unease about the scale of AI-driven market gains.

items.headline: Ramp data shows AI spending stalling as Anthropic nears IPO
items.summary: Corporate card data from Ramp indicates enterprise AI spending has plateaued just as Anthropic approaches its historic public listing. The slowdown raises questions about the durability of AI revenue growth at leading labs.

items.headline: Anthropic says enterprise AI adoption remains in early phases
items.summary: Anthropic's S-1 filing reveals its business is concentrated in technology and software development, with growing footholds in financial services, law and pharmaceuticals. The company characterizes enterprise AI adoption as still in its early stages despite rapid revenue growth.

items.headline: Trump says AI risks manageable, signals openness to guardrails
items.summary: President Trump told CBS's '60 Minutes' that AI risks can be managed but said he 'doesn't mind guardrails.' He expressed openness to working with Democrats on safeguards while keeping the US ahead of China.

items.headline: CodeRabbit uses OpenAI Codex to ship 20x more software
items.summary: CodeRabbit scaled agentic software development using OpenAI models and Codex to govern AI-generated code, shipping 20 times more software with the same engineering team. The case study highlights the enterprise impact of agentic coding tools.

items.headline: Enterprises say AI regulation won't stop corporate innovation
items.summary: Corporate technology leaders say they are pushing ahead with AI plans regardless of how regulation solidifies under Democratic control of Congress and state offices. Democrats are expected to focus on AI safety, including pre-release testing of new models.

items.headline: Regulator warns AI makes university coursework 'impossible' to assess
items.summary: A UK education regulator said AI has made it 'close to impossible' to reliably assess university coursework. The warning intensifies debate over academic integrity and the role of AI-free learning spaces.

items.headline: WSJ: Global economy looks vulnerable to an AI bust
items.summary: Violent swings in stock markets signal that fallout from any AI bust would extend well beyond US shores. The AI build-out has powered global growth amid an energy crunch from the Iran war, leaving the world economy heavily exposed to US data-center investment.
